description: Teach-mode + passive coaching during history. Educational only.

modules.title: Dysphagia history structure
points: Solids-only vs solids-and-liquids from the start is the classic mechanical-vs-motility discriminator.
Progressive course over weeks with weight loss is an alarm pattern until proven otherwise — think malignant stricture.
Always localise: oropharyngeal (cough/choking, nasal regurgitation) vs oesophageal (food sticking retrosternally).

modules.title: Dysphagia alarm features
points: Weight loss, progressive solid-food dysphagia, or a visible lesion/mass warrant prompt endoscopic evaluation to exclude malignancy.
Food impaction episodes support a structural (stricture/ring) cause.

Q000054.why_ask: Solids-only points to a mechanical/structural cause; solids-and-liquids from onset suggests a motility disorder.
Q000054.think: This single answer reorganises the entire differential (stricture/cancer vs achalasia/motility).

Q000055.why_ask: A progressive course over weeks is the classic pattern for malignant stricture; intermittent suggests a ring or spasm.
Q000055.think: Progressive + weight loss + age >50 is a combination that should not be reassured away.

Q000056.why_ask: Localisation (neck vs chest) helps separate oropharyngeal from oesophageal dysphagia.
listen_for: Immediate sticking at the neck vs delayed retrosternal sticking
Q000056.think: Neck-level symptoms with coughing/choking suggest an oropharyngeal (often neuromuscular) cause.

answer_triggers.title: Unlocked: mechanical pattern
points: Consider peptic stricture, Schatzki ring, or oesophageal malignancy.
Progressive solids-only dysphagia with weight loss needs prompt endoscopy.

answer_triggers.title: Unlocked: progressive course
points: Progressive dysphagia is an alarm pattern — do not defer endoscopy.
Ask specifically about weight loss and food impaction.
